results.title: attitude - what are the Common roll angle and roll rate limits for civil flights? - Aviation Stack Exchange
results.content: # what are the Common roll angle and roll rate limits for civil flights? I'm currently doing simulations for eVTOL type of vehicles and for the purpose of controlling the attitude, I'd like to know the common limits for roll and roll rates (more important) that are in place for civil flights. I imagine that there is some at least recommendation that aircraft of a particular type should not exceed this rate, otherwise the passengers can spill their coffee, get sick etc. * $\begingroup$ Are you looking for lower or upper limits (e.g. the aircraft must be able to achieve a roll (rate) of at least XXX, or the aircraft shall not have are roll (rate) exceeding YYY)? ## 1 Answer 1. The minimum roll rate is documented in 14 CFR 23.157 (pre Amdt 64), which is used as an accepted means of compliance for the current 14 CFR 23.2135. As far as I know, there is no regulatory requirement on maximum roll rate. For large transport aircraft, the design target at maximum roll authority is typically around 20 deg/s to 30 deg/s. For example, A320 has a roll rate limit of 15 deg/s at maximum lateral input in Normal Law, while A220 has a roll rate limit of 20 deg/s in Normal Mode. There is no regulatory requirement on maximum roll angle. For reference, the A320 has a maximum commandable roll angle of 67 deg in Normal Law, while the A220 has a limit of 80 deg in Normal Mode. answered Apr 20, 2020 at 15:00.
